subject: EU-West degradation — confirmation request and remediation options
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-payments.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: support@acme-payments.com
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Spike in 503s + latency in eu-west (live production)

Hi Ava,

We started seeing a spike of 503s and token-delivery latency on EU-West around 07:45 UTC — it impacted our payment flow for ~20 minutes. Our ops team captured lots of 5xx responses and elevated latency for completion endpoints. Can you confirm whether this was on Redwood's infrastructure side or a routing issue on our end? We need a service window and evidence to present to our compliance team; also please advise on next steps for potential SLA credits.

Attached: acme_communication_thread.pdf (summary of incidents and screenshots)

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Jones
Head of Engineering, ACME Payments
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 08:28:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike in 503s + latency in eu-west (live production)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the screenshots. I'm sorry you hit this.

Quick answers: we're investigating now. Diego (SRE) is pulling backend metrics and request traces; Lauren is standing by for account next steps. Can you confirm: 1) exact request IDs (if you have them) or a sample of timestamps and paths; 2) whether you observed any consistent correlation with model or route changes on your side?

For the record, we'll aim to provide: confirmed incident window, impacted routes (by model/version), a short impact summary, and preliminary guidance on SLA credit eligibility within 48 hours. If we need an interim hotfix or configuration change we can propose it.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 10:03:45 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike in 503s + latency in eu-west (live production)

Hi all — I've pulled traces and infra metrics for eu-west for the 07:30-08:00 UTC window. Preliminary findings below: 

- Observed a short-lived surge in queue depth on the routing tier starting ~07:43 UTC and returning to baseline ~07:55 UTC.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions (model: redwood-13b-v1) and /v1/generate-text (same model variant).
- Error profile: ~82% of failed requests returned 503 from an autoscaling proxy that hit a resource exhaustion path when burst concurrency exceeded configured thresholds.
- No authentication anomalies or unusual request signatures from ACME's API keys.

I've attached: request_logs_20270220.csv (sampled request IDs + response codes) and latency_snapshot_euwest_20270220.png (CPU/queue graphs).

Next steps I'm proposing: 1) treat as an infrastructure-induced partial outage; 2) confirm exact client impact window with ACME (Sarah, can you confirm whether your observed 07:45-08:05 aligns with logs?); 3) we will prepare an incident summary and preliminary SLA credit calc.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-payments.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, ops-team@acme-payments.com
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 11:01:22 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike in 503s + latency in eu-west (live production)

Thanks Diego — our telemetry confirms a customer-visible degradation from 07:44:30 to 07:56:10 UTC. I attached a quick export of our gateway logs for that window (see acme_communication_thread.pdf earlier).

ACME's compliance group will want: confirmed Redwood incident window, impacted routes, and the quantitative basis for any SLA credit (how you calculate pro-rata credits). Please include explicit statements about whether this maps to our committed availability SLA for our Dedicated plan.

We will expect a postmortem and credit proposal within 72 hours if possible. If remediation requires a config change or best-practice guidance to avoid recurrence, please include that as part of the postmortem.

—Sarah
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike in 503s + latency in eu-west (live production)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the confirmation and for the logs.

Action plan and timeline: 
- Diego will publish an incident summary and evidence bundle (metrics, traces, sampled request IDs) by EOD 2027-02-23.
- We'll produce a postmortem and an SLA credit estimate (methodology and calculation) by 2027-02-25. That will include whether the event meets the Dedicated SLA criteria for downtime and the provisional credit amount.
- We'll include recommended mitigations: adjust autoscaler burst thresholds, enable a short-term routing fallback to the nearest redundant pool, and guidance on client-side retry/backoff best practices.

I've also created a shared doc for transparency: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cExampleDoc (ACME incident workspace). Expect Diego's package in the next few hours.

If ACME prefers an earlier call to walk through the evidence, I can schedule a 30-minute slot tomorrow morning in your timezone.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
